title: Quick check: Introduction to Components

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Introduction to Components”?
options: Component responsibilities belongs in a clear component model with predictable rendering and limited responsibilities.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
questions.answer_key: Component responsibilities belongs in a clear component model with predictable rendering and limited responsibilities.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Introduction to Components: Component responsibilities belongs in a clear component model with predictable rendering and limited responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Component responsibilities?
options: Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Split by cohesive responsibility rather than making one large component or dozens of trivial wrappers.
questions.answer_key: Split by cohesive responsibility rather than making one large component or dozens of trivial wrappers.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Introduction to Components: Split by cohesive responsibility rather than making one large component or dozens of trivial wrappers.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Introduction to Components” complete?
options: Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Introduction to Components: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
